Prayer times

The day, drawn as the sun actually moves.

Home opens on a single arc from Fajr to Isha. The sun sits where it is right now, the next prayer is lit, and a countdown ticks underneath it. No grid of numbers to scan.

  • Accurate for where you are. Times are computed from your location with the calculation method you choose, and update as you travel.
  • Reminders that sound like you want. Adhan, chime, bell or soft. Preview each one before you pick it.
  • Sunrise on the arc too, so you can see how long Fajr has left without doing the maths.
  • A whole-week view when you need to plan around Jumu'ah or travel.

Prayer lock

A phone that waits for you to pray.

When a prayer comes in, Layla can hold your chosen apps behind a mihrab-shaped shield. Social feeds, games, whatever pulls at you. Pray, scan your prayer mat, and they open again.

  • You choose what gets held. Pick the apps and categories; everything else, including calls, stays open.
  • Confirm in two steps. Tap that you prayed, then point the camera at your prayer mat. Layla recognises the mat, marks the prayer, and the shield drops so your apps come back.
  • A nudge, not a cage. Prayed or not, the shield lets go on its own thirty minutes after the prayer begins. Only a confirmed prayer counts toward your streak.
  • "I missed this prayer" is always one tap away. It releases the shield honestly and marks the day.
  • Layla itself is never blocked, so the setting that turns the shield off is always reachable.

Streak

A year of prayer you can hold in one look.

Every day is a dot. Green for five confirmed, amber for a day still open, rose for a prayer missed. Tap any dot to see which prayers it holds. The view turns over quietly each new year.

47days in a row, and counting
  • Today's progress as beads on a string, one for each prayer, filled as you confirm.
  • Step through past years with the arrows, so nothing you kept is ever out of reach.
  • Honest by design. Only a confirmation you tap counts. Nothing is inferred.

Tahajjud

You are not the only one awake.

Tap "I am praying Tahajjud" and a small blue light appears on a globe of the Earth at night. Spin it, zoom in, and the globe hands off to a living map where other lights are glowing too. The night prayer stops feeling solitary.

  • The window is drawn, not listed. Layla divides the night from Maghrib to Fajr into thirds and lights the last one, because that is when Tahajjud is best.
  • Each glow is a five-kilometre area, never a person. Exact locations are never stored or shared.
  • Night stories. Leave a short line about your night for others to find, and read theirs.
  • A globe that is really a globe, with NASA's night-side imagery, city lights and stars, and a proper crescent above it.

Soul

For the moments between the prayers.

The third tab is where the quiet work happens: dhikr, a verse for how you feel, the names of Allah, and a library of duas with their sources.

  • Tasbih that keeps you slow. Tap too fast and Layla gently asks you to take your time. The count is the point, not the speed.
  • Mood. Pick whatever is closest, and turn a deck of verses and hadith chosen for it. Hear each one recited, read why it fits, save it, write a line in your journal, and share it as a card.
  • Names of Allah, one a day, with meaning and a way to sit with it.
  • Duas for morning, evening and everything in between, from the printed pages.

Lock screen and Live Activity

A circular countdown, a two-column grid of today's prayers, and a single inline line for the next one. When a prayer is close, a Live Activity takes the Dynamic Island and counts it down, then hands you the button to confirm.

And the rest

Everything else that lives in Layla.

N

Qibla

A compass that settles on the Kaaba, with a straight bearing from wherever you are.

Home, in one glance

The next prayer, the sun arc, today's beads, a Tahajjud card that glows when the window opens, and your name at the top.

Night dimming

Late screens dim on their own. Mood and Tahajjud are kind to eyes that should be sleeping soon.

Share cards

Verses you save become a card with the mark and the night sky, ready for a story or a message.

Notifications you tune

Per-prayer reminders, minutes-before offsets, and a sound you have actually heard first.

Sign in, or don't

Prayer times, widgets and the streak work without an account. Sign in only for the globe and stories.

Location stays yours

Prayer times are computed on your phone. On the globe, a glow is a five-kilometre cell that expires by itself. Nobody sees where you are.

Nothing is inferred

A prayer counts when you say it does. Layla never guesses from your phone's movement or your screen time.

Made by one person

Layla is built by a single developer who prays with it every day. Every screen is used before it ships.

Keep your prayers with you.

Layla is free on the App Store for iPhone. Install it, tell it where you are, and tonight's window is already drawn.
